transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess I’m here because student health sent me. They said my weight is too low and they won’t clear me for the youth workshops I was supposed to do, which is kind of frustrating because I already had my schedule planned and everything.

They keep saying the number has been dropping, but I don’t know… to me it just feels like what happens when I’m really focused and busy. Like when classes and workshop stuff pile up, I sort of get into this mode where I’m just trying to keep everything organized. So I guess they wanted me to talk to someone before they’ll sign off on it.
Have you been intentionally trying to lose weight or change your eating habits recently?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I’m “trying to lose weight” exactly. It’s more like I plan my day so I don’t have to think about food much. Like I’ll have coffee before studio, and then if I’m around people I might get a few bites of something from the café so it doesn’t become a whole conversation.

And I do avoid certain things… bread, or anything oily. It just feels like if I eat that, I’ve ruined the control I’ve been working so hard to keep. I know that probably sounds dramatic. Studio days are weird too because everyone’s always rushing around and forgetting supplies, and I kind of like having my routine be the one thing that’s predictable.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or upset if your routine around food gets disrupted, or if you end up eating something you normally avoid?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I try not to make it obvious, because then people start watching me, which is the worst. But if something changes, like if the dining hall doesn’t have the “safe” thing I was planning on, or someone wants to go out for dinner, I get this panic feeling.

It’s not even just the food, exactly. It’s like… even the idea of gaining a pound makes me feel like I’m going to lose it. Like if I eat a normal dinner, or something with butter in it, then everyone will somehow be able to see that I lost discipline. Which I know sounds irrational, but in the moment it feels really real.

Sorry, I’m kind of rambling. This happened once with my roommate making pasta and she was being nice, and I just remember focusing on the butter smell instead of anything she was saying.
Do you judge yourself primarily based on your body weight or shape?

I guess… yeah, more than I want to admit. Like, when I look at photos from our showcase, I don’t even really see the artwork first, which is ridiculous because that’s supposed to be the whole point. I zoom in on my arms or my waist, and if I look small enough, I feel like… okay, I’m serious, I’m put-together, I’m doing things right.

And then I’ll get distracted thinking about how the lighting in that room was awful, and how everyone was standing around pretending not to compare their pieces, but I’m doing the same thing with myself in the photo. So… yeah. It’s not just how I look, it feels like it says something about whether I’m in control.
